source_evidence.observation: [PDF p. 5, Section 2, Notation] The paper assumes IEEE 754 floating-point arithmetic, one working precision, no overflow, and permits underflow; F, eps, and eta denote the working-precision numbers, relative rounding-error unit, and underflow unit.

[PDF p. 6, equations (2.1)-(2.4)] The paper defines fl as working-precision evaluation, gives relative-error models for addition and subtraction and relative-plus-eta models for multiplication and division, and defines gamma_m = m eps/(1-m eps), implicitly requiring m eps < 1.
[PDF p. 8, Theorem 3.4] TwoSum gives the exact identity a+b=x+y even with underflow; TwoProduct gives a*b=x+y when no underflow occurs and an error bounded through a 5 eta term when underflow occurs.
[PDF p. 15, Algorithm 4.8] SumK(p,K) performs K-1 error-free VecSum transformations and then a working-precision summation; the paper explicitly notes that SumK with K=2 is Sum2.

[PDF p. 16, Proposition 4.10] For a length-n floating-point vector, 4n eps <= 1, and K >= 3, SumK satisfies |res-s| <= (eps+3 gamma_{n-1}^2)|s| + gamma_{2n-2}^K S, including in the presence of underflow, where s is the exact sum and S is the sum of absolute values.
[PDF p. 20, equation (5.3)] The absolute values of the product and summation remainders, together with the leading accumulated value, are bounded by |x^T y| + gamma_{2n}|x^T||y|.
[PDF p. 21, equation (5.7)] For x^T y != 0, the componentwise relative condition number is cond(x^T y) = 2|x^T||y|/|x^T y|; vector absolute values and comparisons are componentwise.

[PDF p. 23, Algorithm 5.10 and following derivation] DotK constructs a length-2n vector r using n TwoProduct calls and n-1 TwoSum calls, sets r_{2n}=p, and returns SumK(r,K-1). Without underflow, sum_{i=1}^{2n} r_i = x^T y. The derivation invokes Proposition 4.10 and equation (5.3).

[PDF p. 24, equation (5.10) and Proposition 5.11] Under the stated dimension condition, the no-underflow absolute bound is |res-x^T y| <= (eps+2 gamma_{4n-2}^2)|x^T y| + gamma_{4n-2}^K|x^T||y|. Proposition 5.11 also gives the corresponding relative bound, the underflow bound with an added 5n eta, and operation counts.

binders: n is an inferred positive integer dimension: the proposition indexes 1 <= i <= n, and Algorithm 5.10 accesses x_1 and y_1. [PDF p. 24, Proposition 5.11; PDF p. 23, Algorithm 5.10]
K is an integer precision parameter inherited from Algorithm 5.10, whose heading states K >= 3; Proposition 5.11 does not repeat this binder. [PDF p. 23, Algorithm 5.10; PDF p. 24, Proposition 5.11]
x=(x_1,...,x_n) and y=(y_1,...,y_n) are same-length vectors with x_i,y_i in F for every 1 <= i <= n. [PDF p. 24, Proposition 5.11]
res in F is the value determined by running Algorithm 5.10 (DotK) on x, y, and K. [PDF p. 23, Algorithm 5.10; PDF p. 24, Proposition 5.11]
hypotheses: Explicit in Proposition 5.11: x_i,y_i are working-precision floating-point numbers for 1 <= i <= n. [PDF p. 24, Proposition 5.11]
Explicit in Proposition 5.11: 8n eps <= 1. [PDF p. 24, Proposition 5.11]
Inherited from Algorithm 5.10: K >= 3. [PDF p. 23, Algorithm 5.10]
Standing assumption throughout the paper: no overflow occurs. [PDF p. 5, Section 2, Notation]
The first absolute bound and the relative bound are conditional on no underflow occurring. [PDF p. 24, Proposition 5.11]
The alternative absolute bound permits underflow and adds 5n eta. [PDF p. 24, Proposition 5.11]
The relative bound (5.11) inherits x^T y != 0 from the definition of cond(x^T y), although Proposition 5.11 does not repeat it. [PDF p. 21, equation (5.7); PDF p. 24, equation (5.11)]
conclusions: The derivation first states that if 4(2n-1)eps <= 1, then gamma_{4n-2} <= 1 and |res-x^T y| <= (eps+2 gamma_{4n-2}^2)|x^T y| + gamma_{4n-2}^K|x^T||y|. [PDF p. 24, equation (5.10)]

Proposition 5.11 repeats the no-underflow absolute-error conclusion under the stronger displayed assumption 8n eps <= 1: |res-x^T y| <= (eps+2 gamma_{4n-2}^2)|x^T y| + gamma_{4n-2}^K|x^T||y|. [PDF p. 24, Proposition 5.11]

For x^T y != 0, the no-underflow relative-error conclusion is |(res-x^T y)/(x^T y)| <= eps + 2 gamma_{4n-2}^2 + (1/2) gamma_{4n-2}^K cond(x^T y). [PDF p. 21, equation (5.7); PDF p. 24, equation (5.11)]
In the presence of underflow, Proposition 5.11 gives |res-x^T y| <= (eps+2 gamma_{4n-2}^2)|x^T y| + gamma_{4n-2}^K|x^T||y| + 5n eta. [PDF p. 24, Proposition 5.11]
With standard TwoSum and TwoProduct, Algorithm 5.10 requires 6K(2n-1)+n+5 flops, which the paper bounds by less than (12K+1)n flops. [PDF p. 24, Proposition 5.11 following text]
Using TwoSumADD3 and TwoProductFMA instead requires (2K+1)(2n-1) flops. [PDF p. 24, Proposition 5.11 following text]
definitions_and_conventions: The exact target value is d := x^T y = sum_{i=1}^n x_i y_i evaluated as a real number; res is the computed working-precision value. [PDF p. 6, equation (2.3); PDF p. 23, derivation after Algorithm 5.10]
The quantity |x^T||y| is the scalar sum sum_{i=1}^n |x_i||y_i|, obtained by componentwise absolute values followed by the row-by-column product. [PDF p. 20, equation (5.3); PDF p. 21, equation (5.7)]
For m in N, gamma_m := m eps/(1-m eps), with the implicit side condition m eps < 1 whenever gamma_m is used. [PDF p. 6, definition preceding equation (2.4)]

F is the set of working-precision floating-point numbers, eps is the relative rounding-error unit, and eta is the underflow unit; in IEEE 754 double precision the paper gives eps=2^-53 and eta=2^-1074. [PDF p. 5, Section 2, Notation]
For d != 0, cond(d) := 2|x^T||y|/|d|, derived from componentwise relative perturbations of x and y. [PDF p. 21, equation (5.7)]
Algorithm 5.10 defines [p,r_1]=TwoProduct(x_1,y_1); for i=2,...,n it defines [h,r_i]=TwoProduct(x_i,y_i) and [p,r_{n+i-1}]=TwoSum(p,h); it then sets r_{2n}=p. [PDF p. 23, Algorithm 5.10]
Without underflow, the transformed vector satisfies the exact real identity sum_{i=1}^{2n} r_i=x^T y. [PDF p. 23, derivation after Algorithm 5.10]
implicit_context: The quantification over n is not written as n in N with n >= 1, but positivity and integrality are forced by the indexed vectors and loops. [PDF p. 23, Algorithm 5.10; PDF p. 24, Proposition 5.11]
The K >= 3 restriction belongs to Algorithm 5.10 and is inherited by Proposition 5.11 through the phrase result of Algorithm 5.10. [PDF p. 23, Algorithm 5.10; PDF p. 24, Proposition 5.11]

The assumption 8n eps <= 1 implies the preceding sufficient condition 4(2n-1)eps <= 1 for positive n and positive eps; the paper presents the former in Proposition 5.11 and the latter immediately before equation (5.10). [PDF p. 24, equation (5.10) and Proposition 5.11]
The relative statement is meaningful only for a nonzero exact dot product because both its denominator and cond(x^T y) otherwise are undefined. [PDF p. 21, equation (5.7); PDF p. 24, equation (5.11)]

K-fold precision describes the quality of the result rather than use of a K-fold floating-point datatype; all operations are performed in one working precision. [PDF p. 5, Sections 1.2-2; PDF p. 23, Algorithm 5.10]
statement.algorithm_linkage: The contract is specifically for optimized Algorithm 5.10 (DotK), not an arbitrary dot-product implementation: it forms the 2n-entry remainder vector with TwoProduct and TwoSum and calls Algorithm 4.8 as SumK(r,K-1). The last call may be replaced by the paper's equivalent vertical-mode SumKvert. The proof uses the exact transformed sum when there is no underflow, the absolute-sum estimate (5.3), and Proposition 4.10 for K-fold summation. [PDF p. 20, equation (5.3); PDF p. 23, Algorithm 5.10 and following derivation; PDF p. 16, Proposition 4.10]
numerical_model: The standing model is one working precision adhering to IEEE 754, with no overflow and with underflow allowed. [PDF p. 5, Section 2, Notation]

fl denotes evaluation in working precision; addition and subtraction use a relative-error model, while multiplication and division permit an additional perturbation bounded by eta. [PDF p. 6, equations (2.1) and (2.2)]
Addition and subtraction are stated to be exact in case of underflow, which allows TwoSum to remain error-free even then. [PDF p. 6, text preceding equation (2.1); PDF p. 8, Theorem 3.4]
TwoProduct is error-free when no underflow occurs; underflow changes its exact identity by a term whose magnitude is at most 5 eta per call. [PDF p. 8, equations (3.3) and (3.4)]

The paper describes its working-precision accuracy checks as using rounding to nearest, while Proposition 5.11 itself does not restate the rounding mode. [PDF p. 5, Section 1.3; PDF p. 24, Proposition 5.11]
error_notions: The selected conclusion is a forward absolute-error bound comparing computed res with the exact real dot product x^T y. [PDF p. 24, equation (5.10) and Proposition 5.11]
The second no-underflow conclusion is a forward relative-error bound and is defined only when x^T y != 0. [PDF p. 21, equation (5.7); PDF p. 24, equation (5.11)]
The condition number uses independent componentwise relative perturbations of both x and y and therefore contains the factor 2. [PDF p. 21, definition preceding equation (5.7)]
The underflow result is still an absolute-error bound, enlarged by the explicit additive term 5n eta. [PDF p. 24, Proposition 5.11]
norms: The bars around scalars denote ordinary absolute value. [PDF p. 24, equation (5.10)]
For vectors, absolute value and comparison in the condition-number definition are componentwise. [PDF p. 21, text preceding equation (5.7)]
No named vector norm occurs in the bound: |x^T||y| is the scalar absolute dot product sum_i |x_i||y_i|, not notation for a norm product. [PDF p. 20, equation (5.3); PDF p. 21, equation (5.7)]
constants_and_indexing: The gamma index is exactly 4n-2 in every term of the final bounds; its exponent is 2 in the term added to eps and K in the data-dependent term. [PDF p. 24, equation (5.10) and Proposition 5.11]
The coefficient of gamma_{4n-2}^2 is exactly 2, and the relative condition-number coefficient is exactly 1/2. [PDF p. 24, equations (5.10) and (5.11)]
The underflow correction is exactly 5n eta. [PDF p. 24, Proposition 5.11]
The transformed vector has length exactly 2n, with product remainders r_1,...,r_n, summation remainders at indices n+i-1 for 2 <= i <= n, and final leading value r_{2n}. [PDF p. 23, Algorithm 5.10]
The final summation call uses parameter K-1 even though the overall algorithm is described as K-fold. [PDF p. 23, Algorithm 5.10]
The proposition's dimension restriction is 8n eps <= 1, whereas the immediately preceding equation (5.10) uses 4(2n-1)eps <= 1. [PDF p. 24, equation (5.10) and Proposition 5.11]
higher_order_terms: The displayed bounds are finite explicit inequalities and contain no omitted O(eps^j) term. [PDF p. 24, equation (5.10) and Proposition 5.11]
Because gamma_m is the exact rational expression m eps/(1-m eps), its powers are not shorthand for a truncated asymptotic expansion. [PDF p. 6, definition of gamma_m]

The subsequent statement that 2 gamma_{4n-2}^2 is negligible relative to eps and that the error is essentially eps plus a moderate factor times eps^K times the condition number is explanatory prose, not a replacement for the displayed bound. [PDF p. 24, paragraph following Proposition 5.11]
exceptional_values: Overflow is excluded by the paper's standing assumptions. [PDF p. 5, Section 2, Notation]
Underflow is explicitly handled by a separate bound with an additional 5n eta term; the selected no-underflow bound omits that term. [PDF p. 24, Proposition 5.11]
A zero exact dot product is allowed by the absolute bound, but makes the relative bound and cond(x^T y) undefined. [PDF p. 21, equation (5.7); PDF p. 24, Proposition 5.11]

The paper does not specify behavior for NaNs, infinities, signaling values, or signed-zero distinctions; it uses F together with real-arithmetic identities. [PDF p. 5, Section 2, Notation; PDF p. 6, equation (2.3)]

undebatable_constraints: The result concerns equal-length floating-point vectors x and y with n indexed components. [PDF p. 24, Proposition 5.11]
The computed value must be the output of Algorithm 5.10 (DotK), including its remainder-vector transformation and final SumK(r,K-1) call. [PDF p. 23, Algorithm 5.10]
The overall algorithm parameter satisfies K >= 3 as stated in Algorithm 5.10. [PDF p. 23, Algorithm 5.10]
The proposition assumes 8n eps <= 1. [PDF p. 24, Proposition 5.11]
The exact reference value is the real dot product x^T y, not the ordinarily rounded floating-point dot product. [PDF p. 23, exact transformed-sum identity; PDF p. 24, Proposition 5.11]
In the no-underflow case, the absolute bound contains both (eps+2 gamma_{4n-2}^2)|x^T y| and gamma_{4n-2}^K|x^T||y|. [PDF p. 24, equation (5.10) and Proposition 5.11]
Neither the index 4n-2 nor either exponent 2 and K may be shifted or dropped. [PDF p. 24, equation (5.10)]
The relative bound has coefficient 1/2 before gamma_{4n-2}^K cond(x^T y) and requires a nonzero exact dot product. [PDF p. 21, equation (5.7); PDF p. 24, equation (5.11)]
Permitting underflow requires adding 5n eta to the absolute bound. [PDF p. 24, Proposition 5.11]
No overflow is part of the standing model. [PDF p. 5, Section 2, Notation]
|x^T||y| means sum_i |x_i||y_i| and is not an unspecified norm. [PDF p. 20, equation (5.3); PDF p. 21, equation (5.7)]
The theorem contains no big-O remainder or unspecified multiplicative constant. [PDF p. 24, Proposition 5.11]

ambiguities.issue: The cited summation proposition and the DotK parameter range do not align directly at K=3.
ambiguities.evidence: [PDF p. 16, Proposition 4.10] Proposition 4.10 is stated for a SumK parameter at least 3. [PDF p. 23, Algorithm 5.10 and following derivation] DotK is stated for overall K >= 3, calls SumK(r,K-1), and says to apply Proposition 4.10.
ambiguities.impact: For overall K=3, the called SumK parameter is 2, outside Proposition 4.10's printed range. Proposition 5.11 nevertheless inherits K >= 3 from Algorithm 5.10. A formal proof needs a separate K=3 argument, another earlier summation result, or an explicit strengthening of Proposition 4.10; the source passage does not spell this out.

ambiguities.issue: Proposition 5.11 does not restate the nonzero condition required by its relative bound.
ambiguities.evidence: [PDF p. 21, equation (5.7)] cond(x^T y) is defined only for x^T y != 0. [PDF p. 24, equation (5.11)] The relative conclusion divides by x^T y and uses cond(x^T y) without repeating that condition.
ambiguities.impact: Equation (5.11) cannot be applied to an exact zero dot product; only the absolute bound remains meaningful there.

ambiguities.issue: The phrase no underflow occurs is not given an operation-level predicate in Proposition 5.11.
ambiguities.evidence: [PDF p. 24, paragraph preceding Proposition 5.11] The derivation says the only additional underflow error can occur in the initial transformation through the n TwoProduct calls. [PDF p. 24, Proposition 5.11] The proposition itself simply says in case no underflow occurs.
ambiguities.impact: A formalization may use the stronger condition that no operation underflows. Weakening it to exclude only underflow affecting TwoProduct requires encoding the paper's operation-level model and its claim that later underflow introduces no additional error.

ambiguities.issue: The rounding mode is inherited from surrounding numerical conventions rather than repeated in Proposition 5.11.
ambiguities.evidence: [PDF p. 5, Section 1.3] The paper describes working-precision checks in rounding to nearest. [PDF pp. 5-6, Section 2] It then states the IEEE 754 error model. [PDF p. 24, Proposition 5.11] The proposition has no local rounding-mode clause.
ambiguities.impact: A standalone formal statement should either assume round-to-nearest explicitly or assume exactly the error-free-transformation and rounding-model properties used by the proof.

ambiguities.issue: The domain F is not explicitly reconciled with IEEE exceptional values.
ambiguities.evidence: [PDF p. 5, Section 2, Notation] F is called the set of working-precision floating-point numbers and overflow is excluded. [PDF p. 6, equation (2.3)] Operations are related to exact real identities, with no discussion of NaNs or infinities.
ambiguities.impact: The mathematically coherent reading is finite real-valued floating-point inputs and outputs, but exclusion of NaNs, infinities, and related exceptional behavior is implicit rather than stated in Proposition 5.11.

contract_plain_english: For positive dimension n, an inherited integer K >= 3, and working-precision vectors x and y, run the specific optimized DotK algorithm that converts the products and accumulated leading terms into a 2n-entry vector and then calls SumK with parameter K-1. [PDF p. 23, Algorithm 5.10] Under the paper's one-working-precision, no-overflow model and the explicit restriction 8n eps <= 1, if no underflow occurs, the computed res differs from the exact real dot product by at most (eps+2 gamma_{4n-2}^2)|x^T y| + gamma_{4n-2}^K sum_i |x_i||y_i|. [PDF p. 5, Section 2; PDF p. 24, Proposition 5.11] If the exact dot product is nonzero, division by it gives the stated relative bound eps + 2 gamma_{4n-2}^2 + (1/2) gamma_{4n-2}^K cond(x^T y). [PDF p. 21, equation (5.7); PDF p. 24, equation (5.11)] If underflow is permitted, the absolute bound instead has the additional explicit term 5n eta. [PDF p. 24, Proposition 5.11] No asymptotic or big-O term is omitted. [PDF p. 24, Proposition 5.11]
